transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-16 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez (Redwood); Priya Raman, Tom Beckett, Sofia Li (Caravel)

Summary (auto): Crowd check: capacity uplift and AZ-edge onramp, prep for SOW addendum.

[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone thanks for making time, we wanted to run through the commitment options and the AZ geocluster activation that Priya flagged in the last email. How's everyone doing?
[00:18] Priya: Doing well thanks Maya. We had a spike last week, about 2x the normal qps for a short window, so latency got... uh, a little irritable on the west coast users.
[00:32] Tom: Yeah the p95 went up to 380ms on a couple routes,  tail tokens from the conv agent. Not catastrophic but it's annoying for our users.
[00:45] Diego: Got it, thanks for the detail. The AZ-edge geocluster should help—it's basically a proxied region closer to your west coast clients with dedicated pools. We proposed a cluster of four gpus to start.
[01:05] Priya: Can you remind me what the lead time is to provision that? We have security and procurement gates.
[01:12] Maya: Typical provisioning for a hosted AZ geocluster is ~7-10 business days after we sign the addendum and confirm capacity. If you want Dedicated or Private on your VPC it's a bit longer because of the networking -- 2-3 weeks.
[01:28] Sofia: For procurement we need the SOW language to reference region names and the billing reset. Also need any SOC2/ISO certs up front.
[01:36] Maya: Absolutely. We'll attach the security pack. Quick note the product name on the doc sometimes says "Redwood Dedicated" and sometimes "Redwood Dedicated Capacity" — apologies, there's some auto-text mismatch in our template.
[01:50] Tom: No worries. On the technical side, our main question is around KV cache warmup and prefix caching across clusters — will requests routed to AZ have cold cache penalties?
[02:04] Diego: Good question. By default the KV cache is local to the geocluster so there is an initial cold penalty when routing new sessions there. We can enable cross-cluster prefix replication for the top N prefixes (what we usually do for chat-heavy workloads) but that adds some inter-region bandwidth. For your traffic pattern (you showed the histo with long-tail sessions) I'd recommend selective prefix replication for the last 100 prefixes, which reduces cold p95 by ~30% in our tests.
[02:34] Priya: Ok selective replication sounds fine — what's the network egress impact?
[02:40] Diego: It's modest — think tens of megabits for steady state per cluster for your scale. We'll give an exact estimate in the benchmark.
[02:49] Maya: On the commercial side you mentioned wanting a 12-month reserved uplift, can you share the internal approval timeline?
[02:58] Priya: We're aiming to have budget approved in the July 20 exec committee; procurement paperwork likely the week after. Sofia is leading that.
[03:06] Sofia: Yes, we need a PO template and an addendum that spells out region activation, credits if we need to scale down, and an early-exit clause if latency SLAs aren't met during the pilot.
[03:20] Maya: We can add a pilot SLA for the first 60 days with a rollback fence. The commercial team usually proposes a credit schedule tied to p95 latency targets.
[03:31] Tom: What about data residency and KMS? We'll likely want customer-managed keys for some routes.
[03:37] Diego: For Private we support customer KMS/HSM integrations; for hosted we do bring-your-own-key for at-rest encryption in certain plans. I'll attach the KMS integration doc. Note: sometimes our doc refers to KMS as K-M-S in the extractor, ignore that.
[03:53] Priya: On the pilot scope — we'd like a 48-hour soak of production-mirrored traffic routed to AZ edge, then a 1-week canary on two routes with live users. Is that doable?
[04:06] Diego: Yes that's doable. For the 48-hour soak we recommend including KV cache preload with your top prefixes and a synthetic load to simulate the long-tail. We'll instrument token-level latency so we can show delta before/after.
[04:22] Maya: We'll need sample traffic and a small manifest of routes. Priya, can you share those?
[04:27] Priya: I'll send the two route manifests and the sample logs by EOD tomorrow.
[04:32] Sofia: Also we need legal to see the change log for the SOW — any pricing or discounts have to be explicit.
[04:39] Maya: Understood. For pricing we sketched two options: (A) 12-month reserved at 25% discount with commit to N tokens / month; (B) 6-month pilot + convert option at slightly lower discount. Which would you prefer?
[04:54] Priya: Exec is leaning 12-month to get predictability. But they want an escape if SLAs aren't met in the pilot.
[05:03] Maya: We can do that: 12-month with a 60-day performance-based SLA break clause tied to the pilot.
[05:11] Tom: Sounds fair. One more technical ask — can we pin the model family version for the AZ cluster? We want same model weights across regions to ensure consistent outputs.
[05:20] Diego: Yes you can pin to a model version; we also support automatic fallback to a quantized variant if capacity is constrained, but that is opt-in. We'll make the AZ cluster pin to your chosen version.
[05:32] Priya: About fallback — if we pin, will it affect failover?
[05:37] Diego: If you pin strictly, the system won't auto-fallback; we can set a policy that allows fallback only to exact-compatible variants. That avoids regressions.
[05:46] Sofia: For procurement, any special tax implications for reserved capacity across regions?
[05:51] Maya: Tax treatment is usually per-invoice region; we'll have finance note that. I'll have finance loop in.
[05:59] [06:00] -- Middle section: Diego walks through proposed architecture diagram (link shared: https://redwood.example.com/caravel/az-design) --
[06:16] Diego: Here's the quickarch: front door routes with smart routing by geography, dedicated geocluster in the AZ region, local KV cache, optional prefix replication to main region, and metrics exported to your Datadog account. Also optional private control plane for the Private deployment.
[06:35] Tom: On observability — we need token-level traces for the two routes and cost per invocation. Can Redwood expose token-level cost?
[06:44] Maya: Yes, console shows token-level cost and per-route breakdown; we'll add the routes to the dashboard and share a short guide.
[06:52] Priya: For SOC2 evidence — we need audit logs for admin activity and KMS access logs.
[06:58] Diego: Audit logs are available for Dedicated and Private, with retention windows we can extend. KMS access logs require your KMS to push to our ingestion point for Private; for hosted we provide attestations.
[07:11] Priya: Ok. Back to benchmarking — how precise will the latency improvements be? Do you have numbers for a similar customer?
[07:18] Diego: In a recent retail case, adding a west-coast geocluster reduced p95 by ~120ms for interactive routes and reduced token cost ~5% due to reduced cross-region overhead. Your mileage varies. We'll run the same synthetic with your prefixes.
[07:32] Maya: We'll also look at cost delta — adding a cluster increases fixed costs but lowers per-token network egress and can reduce overall latency-based penalties.
[07:42] Sofia: On credits — if the pilot fails, will Redwood provide credits?
[07:46] Maya: We typically include a partial credit schedule for missed SLAs in the addendum. We'll draft it.
[07:53] Priya: I have one compliance question: does Redwood support SCIM provisioning and SSO for admin roles?
[07:59] Diego: Yes, SSO via SAML is supported and SCIM for user provisioning. We'll share the SAML metadata and the SCIM endpoint doc.
[08:10] [08:45] -- quick interruption: background noise, someone says "sorry elevator" --
[09:05] Tom: If we do a Private deployment on our VPC, how long for networking? We have a strict change window.
[09:12] Diego: Typically 2-3 weeks, mostly because of VPC peering, routing, and firewall rules. We provide a detailed network runbook and a checklist.
[09:24] Priya: Ok we'll plan for that. The exec wants a plan B: if the AZ pilot misses targets, do we scale to more capacity in existing region instead?
[09:33] Maya: Yes, we can increase capacity in your main region as a fallback. The addendum will include a scale-up credit to make that smoother.
[09:42] Sofia: For the SOW redlines, are there common clauses we should expect on the Redwood side?
[09:48] Maya: Standard items: data processing addendum, SLA section, termination and exit terms, and IP disclaimers. We'll pre-fill redlines for the SOW to reduce back-and-forth.
[09:59] Tom: About the benchmark logs, what format will you need? JSON lines?
[10:04] Diego: JSONL preferred with request/response timing and route tags. We'll provide a sample schema.
[10:11] Priya: Great. Can you also include a runbook snippet for cache invalidation? We have a nightly job that nukes redis keys occasionally.
[10:20] Diego: We'll include a recommended cache invalidation pattern that works with our prefix replication; basically schedule invalidation windows and use sticky session keys during the canary.
[10:31] Maya: Before we wrap, I'll recap next steps.
[10:35] Maya: Action items — Maya to send addendum and security pack by 7/20; Diego to run benchmark week of 7/26; Priya/Tom to confirm route manifests by EOD 7/17; Sofia to share procurement cadence by 7/19.
[10:52] Priya: That works. One more small asks — do you support reserved token rollovers month-to-month?
[10:58] Maya: We offer limited rollover credits up to 10% of committed tokens per quarter depending on plan. We'll include the exact rollover policy in the pricing appendix.
[11:10] Sofia: Ok if procurement sees the doc next week we can start PO soon.
[11:14] Priya: Thanks team.
[11:17] Maya: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the SOW and the benchmark plan.
[11:21] Tom: Thanks.
[11:23] -- meeting ends --

Notes: Some transcription artifacts: product names occasionally parsed incorrectly (e.g., "Redwood Privatee"), acronyms sometimes expanded weirdly (K-V cash for KV cache). Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/caravel/az-design and security pack link (attached in follow-up email).
